brief: Morgan Stanley's AI beneficiaries basket plunged 16% in a week and is now down 25% from its highs, while the S&P 500 barely moved, framing the question of whether the AI trade's unwind is beginning or has already become washed out. Goldman's trading desk says tech flows remain stretched but buying is starting to reverse, even as hedge funds stay heavily skewed toward semiconductors. High-yield credit spreads for AI-related issuers have widened; historically, AI hyperscaler equities were 15% lower the last time spreads were this wide. Positioning data point to forced de-risking: Morgan Stanley logged a three-standard-deviation selling event (net exposure down to 49%, near yearly lows), Goldman Prime's fundamental long/short net leverage fell 3.2 points, its largest weekly drop since the April 2025 Liberation Day week, to a five-year-low 43.7%, and multi-strategy de-grossing turned alpha negative. The VIX closed above its long-term average for the first time since late July, though Mag 7 implied volatility stays near multi-year lows and hedging remains cheap. Vanda's positioning gauge has stalled since summer as hedge fund exposure rolls over.
